text: If a > 0 and z = $\frac{(1+i)^{2}}{a-i}$,  has magnitude $\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}$, then $z–$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$z=\frac{(1+i)^{2}}{a-i}\times \frac{a+i}{a+i}$

$\Rightarrow z=\frac{(1-1+2i)(a+i)}{a^{2}+1}=\frac{2ai-2}{a^{2}+1}$  

$\Rightarrow |z|=\sqrt{\left (\frac{-2}{a^{2}+1}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{2a}{a^{2}+1}\right )^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{4+4a^{2}}{(a^{2}+1)^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{4(1+a^{2})}{(a^{2}+1)^{2}}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{a^{2}+1}}$.... (i)

Now given $|z|=\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}$

so $\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1+a^{2}}}$ from equation (i)

By squaring both sides

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{5}=\frac{4}{1+a^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow 1+a^{2}=10$

$a^{2} = 9$

$\Rightarrow$ a = $\pm$ 3 

$\because$ (a > 0) then a = 3

Now $z–=\frac{(1-i)^{2}}{3+i}$

= $\frac{\left (1+i^{2}-2i\right )}{3+i}$

= $\frac{\left (1+i^{2}-2i\right )(3-i)}{(3+i)(3-i)}$

= $\frac{(-2i)(3-i)}{(9-i^{2})}$

= $\frac{(-2i)(3-i)}{10}$

= $\frac{-6i+2i^{2}}{10}$

= $\frac{-6i-2}{10}$

= $-\frac{1}{5}-\frac{3}{5}i$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

solution.body:
$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{\sin (p+1)x+\sin x}{x} & x<0 \\ q & x=0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{x^{2}+x}-\sqrt{x}}{x^{\dfrac{3}{2}}} & x>0 \end{array} \right.$

is continuous at x = 0

So $f(0^{–}) = f(0) = f (0^{+}) ... (1)$

$f(0^{-})=lt_{h\to 0}f(0-h)$

$\Rightarrow lt_{h\to 0}\frac{\sin (p+1)(-h)+\sin (-h)}{-h}$

$\Rightarrow lt_{h\to 0}\left [\frac{-\sin (p+1)h}{-h}+\frac{\sinh }{h}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{h\to 0}\frac{\sin (p+1)h}{h(p+1)}\times (p+1)+\lim _{h\to 0}\frac{\sinh }{h}$

= (p + 1) + 1 = p + 2 ...... (2)

Now $f(0^{+})=\lim _{h\to 0}f(0+h)=\lim _{h\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{h^{2}+h}-\sqrt{h}}{h^{3/2}}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{h\to 0}\frac{(h)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\left [\sqrt{h+1}-1\right ]}{h\left (h^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{h\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{h+1}-1}{h}\times \frac{\sqrt{h+1}+1}{\sqrt{h+1}+1}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{h\to 0}\frac{h+1-1}{h\left (\sqrt{h+1}+1\right )}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{h\to 0}\frac{1}{\sqrt{h+1}+1}=\frac{1}{1+1}=\frac{1}{2}$ ..... (3)

Now, from equation (1)

 $f(0^{–}) = f(0) = f(0^{+})$

p + 2 = q = 1/2

So, $q=\frac{1}{2}$ and $p=\frac{1}{2}-2=\frac{-3}{2}$

$(p,q)\equiv \left (-\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2}\right )$

text: Let f : R $\to$  R be differentiable at c $\in$ R and f(c) = 0. If g(x) = |f(x)| , then at x = c, g is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g^{'}(c)=\lim _{x\to c}\frac{g(x)-g(c)}{x-c}$

$\Rightarrow g^{'}(c)=\lim _{x\to c}\frac{|f(x)|-|f(c)|}{x-c}$

$\therefore$ f(c) = 0

$\Rightarrow g^{'}(c)=\lim _{x\to c}\frac{|f(x)|}{x-c}$

$\Rightarrow g^{'}(c)=\lim _{x\to c}\frac{f(x)}{x-c}$ if f(x) > 0

and $g^{'}(c)=\lim _{x\to c}\frac{-f(x)}{x-c}$ if f(x) < 0

$\Rightarrow g^{'}(c)=f^{'}(c)=-f^{'}(c)$

$\Rightarrow$ 2f'(c) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ f'(c) = 0
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text:
If the system of linear equations

x + y + z = 5

x + 2y + 2z = 6

x + 3y + $λ$z = $μ$, ($λ$, $μ$ $\in$ R), has infinitely many solutions, then the value of $λ$ + $μ$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
x + y + z = 5

x + 2y + 2z = 6

x + 3y + $λ$z = $μ$ have infinite solution

$\Delta$ = 0, $\Delta$x = $\Delta$y = $\Delta$z = 0

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & λ \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow 1(2λ-6)-1(λ-2)+1(3-2)=0$

$\Rightarrow 2λ-6-λ+2+1=0$

$\Rightarrow λ=3$

Now, $\Delta x=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 5 & 1 & 1 \\ 6 & 2 & 2 \\ μ & 3 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0$,

 $\Delta$y = $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 5 & 1 \\ 1 & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & μ & 3 \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & μ-5 & 2 \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow μ=7$

$\Delta z=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3 & μ \end{array}\right |=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & μ-5 \end{array}\right |$

$\Rightarrow 1(5-μ+2)=0$

$\Rightarrow μ=7$

So, $λ+μ=10$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text:
The number of 6 digit numbers that can be formed using the digits 0, 1, 2, 5, 7 and 9 which are divisible by
11 and no digit is repeated is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
All six digits 0, 1, 2, 5, 7, 9 are used once; write the number as $a_{1}a_{2}a_{3}a_{4}a_{5}a_{6}$. It is divisible by 11 when $(a_{1}+a_{3}+a_{5})-(a_{2}+a_{4}+a_{6})$ is a multiple of 11.

The two sums add up to $0+1+2+5+7+9=24$, so their difference is even and can only be $0$ or $\pm 22$. A difference of 22 needs a triple with sum 1, which is impossible (the smallest triple sum is $0+1+2=3$). So each triple has sum 12.

The triple containing 0 needs two digits adding to 12, which only 5 and 7 do. The only split is $\{0,5,7\}$ and $\{1,2,9\}$.

$\{1,2,9\}$ in the odd places and $\{0,5,7\}$ in the even places: $3!\times 3!=36$ numbers.

$\{0,5,7\}$ in the odd places: $a_{1}\neq 0$ gives 2 choices for $a_{1}$, then 2 ways for $a_{3},a_{5}$, and $3!$ ways for the even places: $2\times 2\times 6=24$ numbers.

Total $=36+24=60$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot
